memos.headline: CAT at 52-week highs and AMZN surging while MSFT remains in structural downtrend
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. CAT is sitting at its 52-week high with +61.2% over 26 weeks, +41.3% above its 200-day mean, and dominant relative strength vs SPY (+26.3% over 12 weeks)—this is the strongest trend in the group, though the extension raises mean-reversion risk. AMZN has exploded +13.8% over four weeks with RSI at 71.5 and is now +11.7% above its 50-day mean, which looks like a momentum thrust but is stretched enough to warrant caution on new entries. MSFT is the clear laggard: -31.6% drawdown from its 52-week high, trading -21.8% below its 200-day mean with RSI at 38.3 and terrible relative strength (-19.1% vs SPY over 12 weeks)—there is no sign of a bottom yet. I have highest conviction in riding CAT's trend and avoiding MSFT until it can reclaim its 50-day mean near $393.

memos.headline: NVDA and MSFT Lead on Earnings Power; UNH's Near-Zero Margin Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA and MSFT. NVDA posted a 63.1% net margin on $68.1B of quarterly revenue with YoY revenue growth of +73.2% and net income nearly doubling (+94.5%), all on just $8.5B of total debt — an extraordinary profile. MSFT delivered a 47.3% net margin on $81.3B revenue with net income up 59.5% YoY, and its $40.3B debt load is very manageable relative to cash generation. On the other end, UNH's net income collapsed 99.8% YoY to essentially zero on $113.2B of revenue while carrying $78.4B in debt — until I see a credible path back to mid-single-digit margins, I cannot own this name. GOOGL's 30.3% margin and +18% revenue growth on a light $14.8B debt stack also stand out favorably, while XOM and CAT both show contracting earnings despite stable-to-growing revenue, signaling margin pressure I want to avoid.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, +73% revenue growth, minimal leverage at $8.5B debt — best earnings power in the universe.
47.3% net margin with +59.5% YoY net income growth and manageable $40.3B debt make this a high-conviction compounder.
+18% revenue growth, 30.3% net margin, and only $14.8B total debt offer strong risk-adjusted earnings durability.
29.3% net margin and +15.7% revenue growth are solid, though $88.5B debt is the highest in mega-cap tech; would reassess if margins compress below 27%.
Revenue up 13.6% but net income grew only 5.9% on a 9.9% margin — need to see operating leverage improve before getting constructive.
28.4% net margin is respectable for a bank but net income fell 7% YoY; credit cycle trajectory will determine direction.
Only +1.5% revenue growth and -6.7% net income decline suggest limited pricing power; stable but uninspiring.

Revenue down 1.3% and net income down 14.6% with a thin 7.9% margin; commodity headwinds are compressing cash flow.
Despite +18% revenue growth, net income fell 13.9% implying significant margin erosion — cost pressures undermine earnings durability.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% With Sticky Long Rates — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in a pause regime: the upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the past year, while CPI is running at 2.4% y/y — close enough to target to keep the door open but too sticky for imminent easing. Unemployment at 4.3% ticked down 10 bps over three months, signaling a labor market that is softening only gradually, which removes urgency for further cuts. The 10y yield at 4.31% has risen 13 bps over three months even as the front end stayed flat, compressing the 10y-2y spread to 51 bps (down 13 bps in 3m), suggesting the market is repricing term premium higher or pushing out the next cut. This backdrop favors quality duration-sensitive growth names that can compound earnings without needing rate relief, while banks face margin pressure from a flattening curve and cyclicals like CAT face headwinds from tighter financial conditions at the long end. A CPI print above 2.6% y/y or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would change my regime call toward either hawkish re-tightening or emergency easing, respectively.

views.note: High-quality duration growth with recurring revenue benefits from a pause regime where long rates are elevated but stable, and no further tightening is expected.
Resilient consumer franchise in a labor market still near full employment (4.3% UR); moderate confidence given 10y yield drift higher could weigh on multiples.
Ad-driven revenue should hold up with unemployment stable; valuation benefits from pause regime keeping discount rates from rising further.
The 10y-2y spread compressing 13 bps to 51 bps over three months pressures NIM expansion; pause regime limits upside catalyst from further curve steepening.
Staples offer defensive positioning but 2.4% CPI limits pricing power upside while the 4.31% 10y makes the dividend yield less compelling on a relative basis.
Rising long-end rates (+13 bps in 3m) tighten financial conditions for capex-sensitive cyclicals; labor market not weak enough to trigger fiscal stimulus.
Energy is macro-neutral here — no recession signal from labor data but no reflationary impulse either; low conviction without commodity-specific data.
Secular AI capex cycle benefits from stable rates; pause regime at 3.75% removes tail risk of further tightening that would crimp tech multiples.
Consumer spending supported by 4.3% unemployment; AWS growth benefits from same duration-growth tailwind as MSFT in a rate-pause environment.
Defensive healthcare name is rate-insensitive but lacks a clear macro catalyst in a pause regime with no recession imminent.

memos.headline: NVDA Post-Earnings Negativity May Be Washing Out; UNH and GOOGL Leadership Churn Warrants Caution
memos.body: I am working with a limited sentiment dataset today—primarily 8-K filings and one concrete price reaction—so my conviction levels are modest across the board. NVDA's -5.5% price drop on its Feb-25 earnings 8-K is the clearest signal: the negative reaction was sharp, and with six weeks of digestion since then plus a board-level change on Mar-6, the negative tone may be largely priced, creating a potential mean-reversion setup. UNH stands out negatively with three 8-Ks in two weeks (Feb-25, Mar-2, Mar-9), two involving officer departures/appointments, suggesting organizational turbulence that typically generates sustained negative media tone. GOOGL also filed two director departure/appointment 8-Ks (Mar-6, Apr-2) within a month, which I read as governance noise that can weigh on sentiment without offering upside catalysts. AMZN has been the most active filer with four 8-Ks since late February including a material definitive agreement and a Reg FD disclosure just yesterday (Apr-9), suggesting the company is actively managing its narrative—volume of disclosure at this pace can be a positive or neutral signal but not a red flag.

views.note: The -5.5% post-earnings selloff on Feb-25 has had six weeks to be absorbed, and negative tone may be turning—classic sentiment washout setup.
Three 8-Ks in two weeks including two officer departure/appointment filings signal leadership churn that typically sustains negative media tone.
Two director departure/appointment 8-Ks within a month create governance noise but lack a clear directional catalyst.
High 8-K filing cadence including a material agreement and fresh Reg FD disclosure suggests active narrative management, but no clear negative tone shift.
Three 8-Ks spanning Feb-Apr including officer changes and Reg FD are routine for an energy major; no sentiment inflection detected.
Single Reg FD filing in late February is standard pre-conference disclosure with no tone signal.

memos.headline: Oil at $99.62 Signals Structural Energy-Security Stress; Policy Uncertainty Elevated Despite One-Month Pullback
memos.body: I see a geopolitical environment defined by a 69% three-month surge in WTI crude to $99.62/bbl, which I read as reflecting supply-side disruption or sanctions-related tightening rather than a pure demand story, given that the economic policy uncertainty index remains elevated at 293.55 (up 27% over three months even after a sharp one-month decline of 39%). The VIX at 19.49 has cooled from its recent spike but is still 35% above its level three months ago, consistent with markets pricing ongoing geopolitical tail risk. High-yield spreads at 2.90% have tightened modestly over the past month but remain wider than three months ago, suggesting credit markets are not yet signaling an all-clear. I have highest conviction on energy beneficiaries and on avoiding names with concentrated China/export-control exposure; I would need to see WTI retreat below $80 or a concrete sanctions rollback to change my energy view, and a formal easing of semiconductor export controls to upgrade my stance on NVDA.

views.note: Direct beneficiary of near-$100 WTI; two recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-market or operational disclosures consistent with capturing the energy-security premium.
Elevated policy uncertainty index and ongoing semiconductor export-control risk to China make the geopolitical overhang structural; I would need a formal policy easing to upgrade.
Supply-chain concentration in China remains a known risk, but the one-month drop in policy uncertainty suggests near-term tariff escalation may have paused; watching for any new executive orders.
Energy-infrastructure and defense-related capex cycles tend to benefit CAT when oil is near $100 and geopolitical tensions drive reshoring; recent 8-K may relate to order activity.
Multiple recent 8-Ks suggest active disclosure but no clear geopolitical catalyst; elevated oil prices raise logistics costs, partially offset by AWS's domestic positioning.
Banks benefit from steeper curves but the 10y-2y spread has narrowed 13bp over three months; sanctions-related compliance revenue is a modest positive but not enough for a directional call.
